title: Christian Living - Episode 1: Love That Shows Up at Home

parts.style: cheerful for a brand new series, a big smile in the voice, but speaking slowly at a relaxed, unhurried pace with each word clear, then gently settling into a calm, slow bedtime tone
parts.text: Welcome to our brand new SleepFit podcast series! <short pause> This is Christian Living, episode one. <chuckle> I'm David Lee. <short pause> Over the next episodes, we'll spend a few quiet minutes together... thinking about what it means to follow Christ at home, at work, and with the people around us. <short pause> They're made for the end of your day, so you can slow down... and rest. <short pause> And tonight, we're starting with a simple question... <short pause> what does love look like, when you're tired, at home, with the people you see every day?
The apostle Paul gives us a picture of love that's both beautiful... and searchingly honest.

Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up, Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil; Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth; Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things. <long pause>

You've probably heard these verses at a wedding. <short pause> But they're not really about romance, or special occasions. <short pause> They describe the love God asks us to practice in the most ordinary moments of our lives.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Love suffers long, and is kind. <short pause> That's where Paul begins, and it's no accident.

Patience and kindness are what we need most when we're weary... and someone interrupts us, again. <short pause> When the kitchen is finally clean, and someone asks for a snack. <short pause> When you've answered the same question three times already today.

To suffer long means to be slow to irritation... slow to that edge in your voice. <short pause> It means absorbing the inconvenience without keeping score. <short pause> And kindness is the active side of that patience. <short pause> It's the gentleness in your answer, the willingness to help... even when you'd rather not.
Then Paul turns to what love refuses to do. <short pause> Love envies not. It doesn't boast. It isn't puffed up.

At home, envy can be subtle. <short pause> It's the resentment when someone else gets to rest, and you don't. <short pause> It's the comparison that quietly poisons your contentment. <short pause> And pride shows up just as quietly. <short pause> It's the need to be right in every small disagreement. <short pause> Or holding your contribution over someone's head, reminding them what you did.

Love does not behave itself unseemly. It seeks not its own. It is not easily provoked. <short pause> Unseemly behavior is harshness. <short pause> The cutting remark, the rolled eyes, the heavy sigh that says more than words.
Love seeks not its own. <short pause> It doesn't insist on comfort first, or on having the last word, or on getting its way.

And love is not easily provoked. <short pause> That might be the hardest one, at the end of a long day. <short pause> When you're tired, everything can feel provoking. <short pause> The tone someone uses... the task left undone... the small thoughtlessness. <short pause> Love chooses a longer fuse.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Love thinks no evil. <short pause> It doesn't keep a mental record. It doesn't rehearse past wrongs, or assume the worst. <short pause> It gives the benefit of the doubt.

Love takes no pleasure in wrongdoing, but rejoices in the truth. <short pause> It finds no satisfaction in being proven right when someone fails. <short pause> Instead, it's glad when truth and goodness win.

And finally... love bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. <short pause> It bears the weight without complaining. <short pause> It believes the best about the people it lives with. <short pause> It hopes, even when the same issue comes up again and again. <short pause> It endures... which is not the same as gritting your teeth. <short pause> It's a steady presence. A decision to stay tender.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: <exhales> Now, if you're lying here tonight thinking about the ways you fell short of this today... you're not alone. <short pause> These verses show us something true about love. <short pause> And in doing so, they show us how much we need grace.

You can't manufacture this kind of love on your own... especially when you're running on empty. <short pause> But God doesn't hand you a standard, and then leave you to meet it by willpower. <short pause> He gives you himself. <short pause> The same Spirit who inspired these words lives in you... and the fruit of that Spirit is love.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: So tonight, as you let go of the day, bring him the moments you wish had gone differently. <short pause> The impatience. The sharp word. The time you sought your own comfort first. <short pause> He is kind toward you. <short pause> He is patient. <short pause> He does not keep a record of your failings.
And ask him for tomorrow. <short pause> Ask him to love through you in the small moments... the interruptions, the ordinary exchanges that make up a life at home.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Love that shows up at home isn't flashy. <short pause> It's the steady choice to be patient when you're tired... kind when you're empty... hopeful when you're discouraged. <short pause> It's the daily faithfulness that no one applauds... but God sees.

Let's pray. <short pause> Father, thank you that your love for us is patient and kind... that you bear with us, and hope for us, every day. <short pause> Teach us to love the people in our homes the way you love us... not by our own strength, but by your Spirit.
Rest well tonight. <short pause> Goodnight.
